entities.summary:
Angadrisma was a 7th-century abbess and saint, daughter of Robert I, Bishop of Tours, who played a crucial role in the establishment of the monastery at Fontenay-le-Comte. As the abbess of Fontenay, she oversaw the construction of the church and the establishment of the monastery's scriptorium, which produced several illuminated manuscripts, including the 'Liber de Vita Sanctae Radegundae'.

Angadrisma's significance extends beyond her own monastery, as she was a key figure in the transmission of knowledge and culture during the Middle Ages. Her work at Fontenay contributed to the spread of learning and spirituality across Western Europe, influencing the development of monastic education and the preservation of classical texts.

The legacy of Angadrisma can be seen in the many monasteries and churches she founded or influenced, including the Abbey of Saint-Pierre in Angers, France. Her legacy also extends to the many illuminated manuscripts and texts that she helped to preserve and transmit, providing a window into the intellectual and spiritual life of the Middle Ages.

Angadrisma's life serves as a testament to the power of female leadership and the enduring impact of women's work in shaping the course of history.
